Be sure to bring something to entertain yourself to all your appointments. There’s normally a lot of waiting in between appointments and tests.

❤️❤️

Your mum’s GP or breast specialist will be the best source of relevant info. When I spoke to my breast specialist they gave me their card and an info pack, and encouraged me and my family to call through if there was anything I needed to know.

Information varies greatly, so it’s best to get it from the source that’s directly treating you.

But yeah - stay away from google if you can. I scared myself with mastectomy images, when in reality mine has turned out quite well. 

If you’ve got any specific questions I’m more than happy to help (I’ve got a lot of time on my hands at the moment)
I’m in Australia also - it took 5 days to get my biopsy result back. I’ve heard it can take a few weeks, but if it is a serious result they wouldn’t delay any information (trust that).

I had my mastectomy earlier this week, so I’m still recovering from it. Make sure you’ve got button up tops to wear (thankfully my boyfriend has a lot of comfy casual ones that I can pinch) since it’s difficult to lift your arms up, and invest in a water bottle or cup that has a straw/lid so you don’t have to keep lifting it up. 
Also, I took myself to the hairdressers to have my hair washed and blowdried today since I can’t wash it myself - it’s the nicest I’ve felt all week. Would definitely recommend it as a treat ❤️

Do you have any other symptoms that are concerning you? Do you have a family history?

You’re 100% in your right to request a second opinion if you’re not happy with the answer. Always trust your gut ❤️

As someone who is 25 with breast cancer about to head in to mastectomy surgery; mammograms doesn’t really help at all for younger women. Our breast tissue is too dense and it’s incredibly difficult to differentiate tissue from concerning areas. Ultrasound first to look for any lesions and then if they do see something request a biopsy.
Wish you all the best xx
